claims.text: AARO's assurance of 'full access to all pertinent sensitive USG programs' is unfalsifiable as written, because the determination of which programs are 'pertinent' was made by the same SAPCO enterprise that would be the custodian of any concealed program. Reasoning: the reviewer's scope was set by the reviewed.

DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.c: 'The DoD SAP Central Office (SAPCO), under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense, is established and is the primary DoD liaison with agencies of the Executive Branch and the Congress on all issues relating to DoD SAPs ... The Director, DoD SAPCO, shall be a flag officer or Senior Executive Service equivalent appointed by the Deputy Secretary of Defense.'

DoDD 5205.07 (2024) restates it: the Director, DoD SAPCO, 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense, will be a general officer, flag officer, or Senior Executive Service member or equivalent appointed to oversee day-to-day management of the SAP Enterprise,' serves as proponent for SAP policy, as Executive Secretary of the SAPOC and SRG, as Chair of the SSWG, and as 'primary point of contact for congressional matters', and 'Maintains records of DoD SAP information provided to Congress.'
DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1, Enclosure 2, para 3.b: the Director, DoD SAPCO 'Functions as the DoD single point of Congressional liaison concerning SAPs.'

DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Enclosure 3, Note 2: 'The Director, DoD SAPCO, has AAA [access approval authority] for all SAPs unless expressly withheld by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense.' Note 4: the Director 'shall coordinate on PARs for the White House, National Security Council, and political appointees of the Executive Branch.' Note 3: the Director coordinates PARs 'for judicial and other Federal agency personnel for waived programs.'

One office holds: single-point congressional liaison, custody of the record of what was told to Congress, access-approval authority for all SAPs, and the coordination point for White House, NSC, judicial and political-appointee access to waived programs. Every external route into a waived DoD SAP -- legislative, executive and judicial -- transits the same desk, which reports to the Deputy Secretary of Defense and to no one outside the Department. Reasoning stated from DoDD 5205.07 (2010) paras 4.c, 4.e and Enclosure 3 Notes 2-4.

DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.c: DoD SAPCO 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense, is established and is the primary DoD liaison with agencies of the Executive Branch and the Congress on all issues relating to DoD SAPs ... The Director, DoD SAPCO, shall be a flag officer or Senior Executive Service equivalent appointed by the Deputy Secretary of Defense.'
DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 2 para 3.b: the Director, DoD SAPCO 'Functions as the DoD single point of Congressional liaison concerning SAPs.'

DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 2 para 2.k: DoD SAPCO 'Establishes policies and applicable procedures to satisfy reporting requirements for DSS carve-outs, CFIUS, and treaty matters. Provides DSS confirmation of SAP facilities where the DSS has been carved out of security oversight functions.'
DoDD 5205.07 (2024) makes the Director, DoD SAPCO Executive Secretary of the SAPOC and the SRG and Chair of the SSWG, reporting directly to the Deputy Secretary of Defense.

DoD SAPCO is simultaneously the office that (a) writes the criteria for reviewing waived programs, (b) confirms which contractor facilities are carved out of DCSA oversight, (c) is the single point of congressional liaison, and (d) must approve any contractor's provision of SAP material to a member of Congress. Those four functions in one office, reporting to the official who signs the waivers, is the structural definition of a closed loop. Reasoning: enumeration of the four responsibilities from DoDI 5205.11 and DoDD 5205.07.

desc: DoD SAPCO is the exact mechanism at issue on this board. Under DoD Directive 5205.07, reissued 12 September 2024 (cancelling the 1 July 2010 version and incorporating the Deputy Secretary of Defense 'SAP Enterprise Reform' memorandum of 11 July 2023), the Special Access Program Central Office operates 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense', with a Director who must be a general officer, flag officer, or member of the Senior Executive Service and who reports directly to DEPSECDEF. The Director is the proponent for SAP policy, executive secretary of the Department's SAP governance committees - the Special Access Program Oversight Committee and the Senior Review Group - the primary interagency point of contact for SAP matters, and the office that 'coordinates congressional engagement' on SAPs. Every Office of the Secretary of Defense component, military department and defense agency runs its own subordinate OA SAPCO. Directive 5205.07 also imposes the rule that matters most to this record: personnel must 'notify the Director, DoD SAPCO and OA SAPCO directors' before briefing Congress or congressional staff with SAP material, and no contractor may provide SAP material to Congress without specific approval. That is a legally mandated chokepoint sitting between a program manager and an oversight committee. If a legacy recovery and exploitation effort is carried in the SAP architecture, DoD SAPCO holds the list, the accreditation records, the personnel access rosters and the classification guides for it, and DoD SAPCO is the office that would have to be bypassed for a whistleblower to reach a member of Congress lawfully. AARO's March 2024 historical report states that AARO 'established a partnership with the Special Access Program Control Offices for the DoD, IC, and DHS to review programs identified in interviews by name or description' and that 'AARO investigators have been granted full access to all pertinent sensitive USG programs' - a claim of completeness that rests entirely on the SAPCO enterprise having handed over a complete list. No independent verification of that list has been produced to Congress or the public.

claims.text: DoD Directive 5205.07, "Special Access Program Policy," effective September 12, 2024, was approved by Deputy Secretary of Defense Kathleen H. Hicks; it reissues and cancels the July 1, 2010 directive and incorporates and cancels the Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum, "Implementation Guidance for DoD Special Access Program Enterprise Reform," July 11, 2023.

DoDD 5205.07 paragraph 1.2.e provides that the Director, DoD SAPCO, "under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense, will be a general officer, flag officer, or Senior Executive Service member or equivalent appointed to oversee day-to-day management of the SAP Enterprise. The Director, DoD SAPCO reports directly to the Deputy Secretary of Defense."

DoDD 5205.07 paragraph 2.1.b provides: "The Director, DoD SAPCO has jurisdiction over the protection of information contained within DoD SAPs and is delegated TOP SECRET original classification authority for all DoD SAP information for purposes of issuing SAP security classification guides."

DoDD 5205.07 paragraph 2.1.a(5) makes the Director the "DoD primary point of contact for SAP matters with agencies of the Executive Branch, the Judicial Branch, and the Legislative Branch, including support to SAP congressional meetings, hearings, and responses to congressional inquiries, unless otherwise specified by statute or regulation."

DoDD 5205.07 paragraph 2.1.e requires the Director to accredit congressional SAP facilities and to "maintain records of DoD SAP information provided to Congress" — making the same office the conduit for, and the recordkeeper of, what Congress is told.

DoDD 5205.07 paragraph 3.1.g provides: "No DoD contractor entity, contractor employee, contractor representative, or consultant will provide SAP material to any members of Congress or their staff without Director, DoD SAPCO approval."

The SAP Oversight Committee is chaired by the Deputy Secretary of Defense with the Director, DoD SAPCO as Executive Secretary; its membership includes USD(R&E), USD(A&S), USD(P), USD(C)/CFO, USD(I&S), the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the DoD General Counsel, DCAPE, the DoD CIO, the Under Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force, ASD(SO/LIC), and the service vice chiefs.

DoDI 5205.11 paragraph 1.2.b provides that only the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense may alter the tier-1 SAP architecture, while "The Director, DoD Special Access Program Central Office (SAPCO) may approve establishment and disestablishment of DoD SAPs at tiers 2 and below."
DoDI 5205.11 requires the SAPOC's annual review to assess "All waived DoD SAPs to determine the need for continued waived status."

DoDI 5205.11 provides that Access Approval Authority for non-waived SAPs may be delegated to component SAPCO staff, while "AAA for waived SAPs may be delegated to the SAPCO Deputy Director or alternate designee," and that "DoD SAPCO will coordinate on PARs for judicial and other federal agency personnel for waived programs."

DoDI 5205.11 assigns DoD SAPCO the duty to notify the congressional defense committees of changes to CPI protected by DoD SAPs, and the intelligence committees for intelligence or intelligence-related CPI, and to report proposed classification changes or declassifications with a description, the reasons, and notice of any planned public announcement.

DoDI 5205.11 states that Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency oversight for administration of the National Industrial Security Program "will be phased out in July 2029 in accordance with the carve-out provision of DoD Instruction (DoDI) 5220.31" — removing an independent industrial-security inspector from the SAP contractor base.

Major General David W. Abba, U.S. Air Force, served as Director of the DoD Special Access Program Central Office; a March 2023 memorandum signed by Abba stated that AARO was authorized to receive information relating to sensitive U.S. Government information and activities, and was released under FOIA case 24-F-0266. Abba also participated with then-acting AARO director Tim Phillips in a classified UAP briefing for members of Congress on April 17, 2024.

Former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick stated in a July 17, 2024 interview that he had briefed and testified to members of Congress "with the SAPCO director and the CAPCO director from ODNI" and that all of the alleged hidden programs "have turned out to be other things that have nothing to do with extraterrestrial reverse engineering. And all of them have been reported to Congress."

Waived SAPs remain subject to congressional oversight.'
The Director, DoD SAPCO operates 'Under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense (DepSecDef)' — not the Secretary of Defense and not the USD(I&S).

DoD SAPCO 'Functions as the DoD single point of congressional liaison concerning SAPs and verifies that the congressional offices that are approved to process and store DoD SAP information implement the security requirements in this issuance.'
The Special Access Program Oversight Committee conducts an annual review of DoD SAPs that expressly includes assessing 'All waived DoD SAPs to determine the need for continued waived status.'

The SAPOC convenes at the direction of the Deputy Secretary of Defense; the Senior Review Group convenes at the direction of the Deputy Secretary of Defense or on the recommendation of the Director, DoD SAPCO.

claims.text: A new SAP umbrella may not be created until the Director, DoD SAPCO has notified the congressional defense committees in writing and 30 calendar days have passed after delivery of the notification.

Under 10 U.S.C. 119(e), when the Secretary of Defense waives a SAP reporting requirement, the information and the justification for the waiver go 'jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees' — a channel of twelve members given the six bodies defined in subsection (g).

claims.text: The requirement in 10 U.S.C. 119(a) and (b) that the Secretary of Defense submit annual reports to the defense committees on all special access programs was terminated effective 31 December 2021 by section 1061 of Public Law 114-328.
Four Principal Staff Assistants are designated DoD SAP Oversight Authorities: USD(R&E), USD(A&S), USD(P), and USD(I&S).

USD(I&S) 'Serves as the primary interface for the Director of National Intelligence's Controlled Access Program Central Office for all relevant issues,' linking the DoD SAP architecture to the Intelligence Community CAP architecture at a single office.

DoD Component heads with cognizant authority over SAPs may 'Initiate actions to replace DCSA security cognizance activities, also known as "carve out"' and must 'Notify DCSA of activities or areas for which DCSA is relieved from inspection authority' — removing the default government industrial-security inspector from contractor facilities.

Eric Burlison's 22 May 2026 interrogatories to MITRE demand identification of every SAP, Controlled Access Program, ACCM, Managed-Need-To-Know codeword, DOE Restricted Data/Formerly Restricted Data compartment and SIGMA category touching UAP records, and for each, 'whether the program was reported to the appropriate congressional committees.'

SAP governance is layered as SSWG to SRG to SAPOC, with disagreements referred upward, and the Deputy Secretary of Defense issuing the final approval or disapproval memorandum, a copy of which the Director, DoD SAPCO distributes to the CA SAPCO and SSWG.

connections: Administers the waived unacknowledged SAP mechanism created by 10 U.S.C. 119(e); controls congressional access under DoDI 5205.11 section 7.
Reports directly to the Deputy Secretary of Defense — Kathleen H. Hicks signed the 2024 reissuance and chaired the SAPOC.
Maj. Gen. David W. Abba (Director) is the signatory of the March 2023 memorandum on which AARO's authority to interview cleared witnesses, including David Grusch, rested.
Paired in Kirkpatrick's account with ODNI's CAPCO (Controlled Access Program Coordination Office) as the two offices that jointly told Congress the alleged programs do not exist.
Absorbed the Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum of July 11, 2023 on 'DoD Special Access Program Enterprise Reform' — issued three days before the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act was unveiled.
Also Executive Secretary of the Special Technical Activities Oversight Committee established by the November 21, 2020 Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum.
Directly targeted by FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687, which conditions funding for UAP activities 'protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitations' on disclosure to Congress.
Deputy Secretary of Defense — sole authority over SAPOC/SRG convening and final SAP governance decisions; the Director, DoD SAPCO reports to this office directly (DoDM 5205.07 Para. 2.4).

USD(I&S) — DoD Senior Security Official, SAP Oversight Authority, and primary interface to the DNI's Controlled Access Program Central Office; also the office to which the AARO Director reports on all administrative matters under 50 U.S.C. 3373(b)(3)(B)(i).
10 U.S.C. 119 — the statute the waiver authority runs on; its annual SAP report requirement terminated 31 December 2021.
Rep. Anna Paulina Luna and the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets — locked out of UAP SAP material by HASC/HAC-D read-in rules per her 9 September 2025 opening statement.

Rep. Eric Burlison's 22 May 2026 MITRE interrogatories — first congressional demand to a contractor to enumerate SAP/CAP/ACCM/MNTK/SIGMA participation against UAP subject matter and state congressional reporting status.
DCSA (Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency) — the inspection authority that 'carve out' removes from SAP contractor facilities.

David Grusch — testified 26 July 2023 that a concealed multi-decade crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering effort was withheld from proper congressional oversight; the waived-SAP construct is the only lawful architecture in which that could be true.

AARO's Historical Record Report Volume 1 (8 March 2024) — asserts interviewees 'mistakenly associated' authentic classified programs with extraterrestrial activity, an argument that concedes the existence of authentic classified programs adjacent to the allegations.
dossier.denialPosture: DoD SAPCO does not speak publicly under its own name. Its position enters the record through others: the Abba memorandum authorizing AARO to receive sensitive information, and Kirkpatrick's account of the SAPCO director appearing alongside him before Congress to say that every alleged hidden program had been checked, was something else, and had already been reported.
dossier.narrative:
DoD Directive 5205.07, "Special Access Program Policy," was reissued on 12 September 2024 over the signature of Deputy Secretary of Defense Kathleen H. Hicks. It cancels the July 1, 2010 version and, importantly, incorporates and cancels the Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum of July 11, 2023, "Implementation Guidance for DoD Special Access Program Enterprise Reform." That reform memorandum was issued three days before the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act was unveiled and eight days before the Senate added it to the NDAA. The companion issuance, DoD Instruction 5205.11, was reissued the same day.

The Directive creates four governance bodies and one office. The SAP Oversight Committee is chaired by the Deputy Secretary of Defense and includes the four Under Secretaries who serve as SAP oversight authorities — Research and Engineering, Acquisition and Sustainment, Policy, and Intelligence and Security — plus the Comptroller, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, the DoD General Counsel, the Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation, the DoD Chief Information Officer, the Under Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force, the ASD for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict, the Vice Chiefs of the Army and Air Force, the Assistant Commandant of the Marine Corps, and the Vice Chiefs of Naval and Space Operations. The Director of DoD SAPCO is its Executive Secretary. Below it sits the Senior Review Group, which the Directive pointedly says "has no designated individual as the Chair," and below that the SAP Senior Working Group, chaired by the Director of DoD SAPCO, whose voting members are the SAPCO directors of the four oversight-authority offices, the military departments, SOLIC, and the Joint Staff.

The Director's own portfolio in section 2.1 of the Directive is broader than the governance role. He is the "DoD-designated proponent" for SAP policy; the oversight authority for SAPs designated by the Deputy Secretary, "including those protecting capabilities and information shared with the DoD by foreign governments"; the cognizant authority for SAPs designated by the Deputy Secretary, for DoD components not supported by another SAPCO, for foreign-government-shared capabilities, and for "SAP studies, portfolios, and associated access management structures involving DoD SAPs"; and the DoD primary point of contact for SAP matters with all three branches of government, "including support to SAP congressional meetings, hearings, and responses to congressional inquiries." He is also Executive Secretary of the Special Technical Activities Oversight Committee established by a Deputy Secretary of Defense memorandum of 21 November 2020. He publishes and maintains security classification guides for all DoD SAP umbrellas and is delegated TOP SECRET original classification authority for all DoD SAP information for that purpose. He maintains the single authoritative repository of SAP personnel access and facility accreditation. He accredits congressional SAP facilities and maintains the records of what SAP information Congress received.

Paragraph 3.1.g of the Directive is the sentence to underline: "All personnel accessed to DoD SAPs will notify the Director, DoD SAPCO and OA SAPCO directors through their SAP CA SAPCO in a timely fashion when briefing or providing DoD SAP material to any member of Congress or their staff. No DoD contractor entity, contractor employee, contractor representative, or consultant will provide SAP material to any members of Congress or their staff without Director, DoD SAPCO approval." A contractor employee who believes a program is being illegally concealed from Congress must, under this rule, ask the office that administers that program for permission to tell Congress about it.

DoDI 5205.11 supplies the operating mechanics. Only the Secretary or Deputy Secretary may alter the tier-1 architecture; the Director of DoD SAPCO may approve establishment and disestablishment of SAPs at tier 2 and below. New CPI enters through a "SAP project" assigned a number in the TR umbrella, and if a decision is not reached in 210 days it transfers automatically toward termination absent a waiver from the Secretary or Deputy Secretary. Access Approval Authority for non-waived SAPs may be delegated to component SAPCO staff; "AAA for waived SAPs may be delegated to the SAPCO Deputy Director or alternate designee." DoD SAPCO coordinates on personnel access requests for judicial and other federal agency personnel for waived programs — that is, the office decides which judges and which agencies get read in. The SAPOC's mandatory annual review must assess, among other things, "All waived DoD SAPs to determine the need for continued waived status."

The office intersects the UAP record at three documented points. In March 2023 Major General David W. Abba, then Director of DoD SAPCO, signed a memorandum — released to The Black Vault in FOIA case 24-F-0266 — stating that AARO was authorized to receive information relating to sensitive U.S. Government information and activities, the instrument on which AARO's repeated attempts to interview David Grusch rested. On 17 April 2024 Abba appeared alongside acting AARO director Tim Phillips in a classified UAP briefing to members of Congress. And in July 2024 former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick described briefing and testifying to members of Congress "with the SAPCO director and the CAPCO director from ODNI," saying that they had gone through everything and that none of the alleged hidden programs were what witnesses claimed.

That last item is the denial, and it is a good one to catalogue precisely because of who is standing next to whom. The office that administers waived SAPs, the office that controls contractor communication with Congress, and the office that keeps the records of what Congress was told, went to Congress to say there is nothing there.
openQuestions: Whether DoD SAPCO's records of 'DoD SAP information provided to Congress' have ever been examined by an independent body, and whether they would show what the twelve recipients of any waived-SAP notification actually received.
The full text and classification markings of the March 2023 Abba memorandum, and whether it authorized disclosure to AARO of waived-SAP information or only of non-waived material.
Whether any request has been made under DoDD 5205.07 para 3.1.g by a contractor employee seeking approval to take SAP material to Congress, and how such requests are adjudicated and logged.
Who succeeded Abba as Director of DoD SAPCO and what that officer has told Congress about UAP.
What the July 11, 2023 SAP Enterprise Reform memorandum actually directed, given that it has now been cancelled and absorbed into DoDD 5205.07 without separate publication.
Which judicial personnel have been granted access to waived DoD SAPs, and in connection with which litigation.
How many waived SAPs currently exist, and what is the aggregate dollar value? No unclassified figure is published, and the annual report that would have supplied one terminated 31 December 2021.
Which office maintains the master list of waived SAPs reviewed annually by the SAPOC, and does that list carry program nicknames releasable to Congress under DoDI 5205.11?
How many DoD contractor facilities currently operate under 'carve out' with DCSA relieved of inspection authority, and which Components initiated them?
Has any DoD SAPCO Director ever certified to the defense committees that no UAP- or recovered-materials-related SAP exists? No such certification is in the public record.

Did the 31 December 2021 termination of the 10 U.S.C. 119 annual report result from a deliberate legislative choice or from the generic reporting-requirement sunset in section 1061 of P.L. 114-328? The statutory note does not say.

What is the relationship, if any, between the DoD SAP architecture and DOE SIGMA compartments for nuclear weapons design information, which Burlison's letter treats as potentially co-located with UAP material?
dossier.whatItIs: The DoD Special Access Program Central Office is the headquarters element that runs the Department of Defense's entire special access program enterprise. Its Director operates under the authority, direction and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense, reports directly to the Deputy Secretary, serves as Executive Secretary of the Special Access Program Oversight Committee and Senior Review Group and Chair of the SAP Senior Working Group, and holds delegated TOP SECRET original classification authority for all DoD SAP information. It is also the Department's single point of contact for SAP matters with the Executive, Judicial and Legislative branches.
dossier.whyImplicated: If a legacy program exists inside the Department of Defense, DoD SAPCO is the office that knows where it sits in the architecture, who is read in, and what Congress has been told. Three provisions of the governing issuances make this office load-bearing rather than merely administrative. First, DoDD 5205.07 paragraph 3.1.g bars any DoD contractor entity, employee, representative or consultant from providing SAP material to any member of Congress or their staff without the Director's approval — a regulatory chokepoint sitting directly across the path of every contractor whistleblower. Second, the Director accredits congressional SAP facilities and "maintains records of DoD SAP information provided to Congress," which makes SAPCO both the conduit and the recordkeeper of its own conduct. Third, under DoDI 5205.11 the Director may approve the establishment and disestablishment of SAPs at tier 2 and below on his own authority with SSWG concurrence, meaning a single flag officer or SES can create and dissolve compartments. In March 2023 the then-Director, Major General David W. Abba, signed the memorandum that authorized AARO to receive sensitive U.S. Government information and effectively released NDA-bound personnel to speak to AARO — the single most consequential document in the government's handling of the whistleblower question, and it came from this office.

entityInfo.desc: The mechanism, stated plainly. Three documents define the space in which a concealed program could lawfully live. (1) 10 U.S.C. 119: annual SAP report to the four defense committees by 1 March; new-SAP notification by 1 February; 30 days notice before initiation - unless the Secretary waives it, in which case the information and the waiver justification go 'jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees'. Eight members. (2) DoD Directive 5205.07, reissued 12 September 2024, cancelling the 1 July 2010 version and incorporating the DEPSECDEF SAP Enterprise Reform memorandum of 11 July 2023: DoD SAPCO sits under the authority, direction and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense; its Director is a GO/FO/SES reporting directly to DEPSECDEF, is executive secretary of the SAP governance committees, and 'coordinates congressional engagement'; and any person briefing Congress or congressional staff with SAP material must notify the Director, DoD SAPCO first, while contractors may not provide such material to Congress without specific approval. (3) The read-in practice described on the record by Chairwoman Anna Paulina Luna on 9 September 2025: a non-committee member must be approved by the chairman and ranking member of both HASC and HAC-D. Composed, these produce a structure in which the office administering a program is notified before the overseer is briefed, the contractor holding it is barred from talking to Congress, and the members entitled to know can be counted on two hands. Nothing in that sequence requires anyone to break the law.
